title: Nested binary64 all-reduction workload evidence
objective: Add an authentic scalar and vector grid workload plus exact checked nested-binary64 all-reduction feasibility evidence with 11 complete-public ABBA pairs and independent oracles; do not claim a compiler route.

oracles: independent CPython scalar and vector grid digests
Sage.js O0 and O2 exact differential

handoff.summary: Added the CPython-parseable binary64 grid profile source, a complete-public O2 feasibility runner, and focused tests. The runner mechanically derives the checked V8 candidate by replacing only the scalar/vector nested all(math.isfinite(...)) expressions in the exact public source; its guards authenticate builtin identities, dense list/row or fixed-pair shapes, both strict-float representations, source-order short circuit, periodic intrinsic interrupts, and one untouched dynamic fallback. It also executes a separate checked scalar float-materialization candidate as raw same-workload negative evidence. Independent CPython plus Sage.js O0/O2 and both checked targets agree on complete output digests. The report preserves raw ABBA rows, target dispositions, scalar primary/vector heldout phases, period/class-unit obligations, a non-consumable smoke policy, and the exact catalog document.
risks: Only non-promotable smoke and a borrowed-build 3-pair probe were run in this lane; the clean integrated 3-warmup/11-pair standard receipt is still required.
The borrowed-build 400x400/100x100 3-pair probe measured 1.079x scalar and 1.098x vector median ratios; the full standard distribution must decide materiality.
The required period and class/unit neighboring workloads are explicitly not run and must be supplied before promotion.
Broad build, compiler, architecture, browser, and VM gates are intentionally deferred to the integration lane because this lane borrowed the current base dist only for non-promotable smoke.
